message.content:
Here are some of the most popular and highly regarded sushi restaurants in Tokyo, ranging from Michelin‑starred establishments to well‑known local favorites:

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights | Michelin Stars |
|------------|----------|------------|----------------|
| **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Ginza (original) & Roppongi | Legendary chef Jiro Ono; famed for meticulous nigiri and traditional Edomae style. | 3 |
| **Sushi Saito** | Minato | Intimate setting, 3 Michelin stars; known for precision and high‑quality fish. | 3 |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Ginza | 3 Michelin stars; elegant plating and seasonal ingredients. | 3 |
| **Sushi Mizutani** | Ginza | 2 Michelin stars; focuses on simplicity and freshness. | 2 |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Famous for long lines but worth it for fresh tuna and sashimi. | — |
| **Sushi Zanmai** | Multiple locations | Casual, open‑air counter, great value, 24‑hour service. | — |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza | 2 Michelin stars; renowned for its “Kurobuta” pork and high‑grade fish. | 2 |
| **Sushi Sawada** | Ginza | 1 Michelin star; known for its “Omakase” tasting menu. | 1 |
| **Sushi Tsubaki** | Ginza | 1 Michelin star; offers a refined omakase experience. | 1 |
| **Sushi Iwa** | Shinjuku | 1 Michelin star; praised for its creative rolls and fresh fish. | 1 |
| **Sushi Kanda** | Minato | 3 Michelin stars; celebrated for its meticulous preparation and seasonal focus. | 3 |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Ginza | 1 Michelin star; known for its “Omakase” menu featuring seasonal fish. | 1 |
| **Sushi Shun** | Ginza | 1 Michelin star; offers a modern take on traditional sushi. | 1 |
| **Sushi Saito** | Minato | 3 Michelin stars; known for its intimate setting and exceptional quality. | 3 |

### Tips for Visiting

- **Reservations:** For Michelin‑starred spots, book months in advance.  
- **Dress Code:** Many high‑end sushi bars require smart attire.  
- **Payment:** Some places accept only cash or credit cards; check ahead.  
- **Tipping:** Not customary in Japan; service charges are usually included.

Enjoy your sushi adventure in Tokyo!
